title: Know what your factory is making
new: Select a factory: NOW PRODUCING shows the unit, its bar and the seconds left; NEXT shows what comes after it, with repeats merged as ×N; +N more lists the rest. QUEUE n / 9 says how full it is.
Click or right-click NOW PRODUCING to cancel that unit. Right-click a unit's button to cancel the last one of that kind. Hold Shift to queue or cancel five.
Slow or stuck production says why: the seconds turn red under low power, and NOW reads Exit blocked when the unit cannot get out.
The top right shows one chip per producer: click to select it, double-click to go there. F7 (fn+F7 on a Mac keyboard) switches the chip bars between flat and upright.
Every unit button has a picture now, and the $ coin is gone: a cost you cannot afford is red.

try.text: Queue a mix at one factory, look away for 30 seconds, then select it. Can you say within a few seconds what it makes, roughly when, what is next and how many wait?
Hold Shift and click a unit's button to queue five, then Shift-right-click it to cancel five
Cancel the unit in production by clicking NOW PRODUCING, and one queued unit by right-clicking its button
With two or more producers busy, click a chip at the top right, then double-click another
Press F7 a few times on a busy base and compare the flat and upright bars
Let power run low while a factory works, and read the NOW row

questions.text: I could tell at a glance what my factory was making and what came next
I never cancelled something by accident
The chips at the top right helped me keep my producers busy
I preferred the flat bars over the upright ones

title: Build from the dock
new: The build buttons now sit in a card at the bottom right. Select your builder, press Q or click Build, then pick a building. Each button shows its key in the corner: Q Power Plant (USA or China; FRC has no Power Plant), E Barracks.
V or the Back button leaves the build grid. Esc does too. Esc backs out one step at a time: a placement first, then the build grid, then your selection, then the menu.
A factory's card has the units to queue, each on its own key.
You start with your builder already selected.
W A S D no longer pan the map. Use the arrow keys.

The top strip is two small boxes, credits and power. Point at something and the numbers it changes show an arrow and what you would have after it. If you cannot afford it, the number goes below zero in red.
A producer's panel shows its queue as tiles; click one to cancel, or right-click the unit's button.
H and Space glide to the HQ or the last attack; in a window, edge scroll keeps going just past the edge.

try.text: From Play, use only the mouse: no keys. Build your first building. Observer: note the time from the start to that first building and where the player looked
Build a Power Plant (USA or China; FRC has no Power Plant): press Q, then Q again, then place it
Build a Barracks by clicking: Build, then Barracks, then place it

Open the build grid and leave it with V. Open it again and leave it with Esc. Then press Esc with a building armed and see what it does first. Observer: the build card has no title; note whether the Back button alone was clear (if not, label it Back · Build)

After a building is placed, deselect your builder by clicking empty ground, then carry on. Observer: note the time to the next build order, the seconds the card stays empty while the player could afford a building, and ask what they expected to find with nothing selected
Move the pointer to the screen corner where the Back button sits, then click Back. Note whether the map scrolled while you aimed
Select a factory and queue units from its card by key and by click
Queue three units, then cancel one by clicking its tile and one by right-clicking its button
At the start your builder is already selected. Note whether that helped or got in the way
Pan with the arrow keys. Note anything you missed without W A S D
Point at a building you cannot afford and read the top strip

questions.text: Building by key was quick
I always knew how to back out, with no title on the card
Starting with the builder selected helped, and after I deselected it I knew how to get the build buttons back
I did not miss W A S D for panning, and the screen edge never scrolled when I did not want it
The top strip told me what I could not afford

title: See your selection
new: Credits (and power, if your side uses it) sit on the top edge. Point at a buy button or place a building and the numbers it changes show an arrow and what you would have after it.
Select something and a panel at the bottom left shows it: one unit, a group by kind, a building, a building going up, a supply pile or an enemy.
A refused order shows the game's reason on a line at the bottom of the screen, between the panel and the buttons (still in the game's own words; plainer words come next).

The bottom-right buttons follow your selection: Build for one builder, Attack move and Stop for armed units, Unload for a loaded vehicle or Tunnel Hub. Keys are on the buttons; Unload moved from U to F. A factory's queue sits above its buttons; click a tile to cancel it. E no longer produces: press the key shown on the button.
Right-click acts on what is under the pointer: move, attack, collect from a pile, or enter a Scout Car or Tunnel Hub. Esc or a right-click cancels a placement or an attack move.

try.text: Select a mixed group, drop one kind with the panel's kind rows, then try to get it back
Select your collectors (trucks, helicopters or Laborers) and read what the panel says they are doing
Click an enemy unit and a supply pile
Point at a building you cannot afford and read the top strip, then try to place it; note whether you saw the line at the bottom
Select two builders, or a builder and a tank, and look at the buttons; note anything you expected to find
Put infantry in a Scout Car or Tunnel Hub, then unload with F or the Unload button
Pull the builder off a building going up, then get it finished. Note whether you knew how
Queue six or more units at one factory, then cancel one you picked

questions.text: I could always tell what I had selected
The HUD and the open checklist never took a click I meant for the battlefield
The bottom-right buttons showed what I could do with my selection
When I pointed at a buy button, I could tell the top numbers showed what I would have, not what I had
I could cancel the queued unit I meant and never cancelled one by accident

title: Notes that never block
new: The playtest notes live in one panel: checklist, questions and markers, any time during or after a match. The key left of 1 (shown in the panel title) opens it.
The panel never pauses or blocks play and has no Save button: notes save themselves. Only the marker box (N) pauses an offline match while it is open.
On desktop your notes are filed when you quit or close the window; in the browser they download when you come back to the launcher.

try.text: Type a comment into one of the panel's fields mid-match, then click the battlefield and give an order
Press N, pick a kind and Save, finish the match, then type a comment under the marker

Answer the questions first. Desktop: type in a field, leave the cursor in it, close the window, restart and look in the Notes folder shown on this card. Browser: go back to the main menu and look in your downloads.

questions.text: Saving my notes never got in my way
I knew where my notes would go
I never had to think about saving

title: Result panel
new: After a match the panel shows the match length and, for every player, units built, units lost and buildings lost.
If your opponent leaves mid-match you win, and the panel says so.
Leaving an online match now says what it means.

try.text: Finish a match and read the numbers on the panel
Online, have your friend leave in the middle of a match
Online, open the menu and choose Back to main menu

questions.text: I could read the numbers at a glance
When my opponent left, I knew what had happened
The leave question told me what would happen

title: Play again
new: After a match, Play again starts a new one with the same friend and the same link.
A waiting match stays open for 15 minutes, with a countdown.
Enter joins a code; Cancel or Esc stops connecting.

try.text: Finish an online match and press Play again on both sides
Create a match, switch to another tab or app for a minute, then let your friend join
Press Cancel while connecting

questions.text: Starting a second match was quick
The result panel told me what was going on
Waiting for my friend felt safe

new: The menu has a sidebar: Play, Join, Settings, Credits.

title: Every order heard
new: Units answer every order with a short voice line.
The menu has sections; the relay URL sits under Advanced.
Match music is shuffled each match.
